Brave Rewards: Common Questions about Rewards

How do I make contributions to websites and content creators with Brave Rewards?

Brave Rewards allows you to contribute to creators with:

  • On-demand contributions
  • Recurring contributions

On-demand contributions

On-demand contributions are like tips. Visit a Verified Creator website or channel, then press the BAT icon in the URL bar. Verified Creators are marked with a blue checkmark.

Then, press “Contribute”. This will open up the contribution window, which will allow you to select an amount you’d like to contribute.

Then, press Send BAT. 

Recurring contributions

To automatically send a contribution of some amount every month to a creator, toggle on the “recurring contribution” option when making an on-demand contribution. Your contribution will recur every 30 days automatically. 

You can cancel your monthly recurring contribution at any time by navigating to brave://rewards.

Please note, recurring contributions are only available for custodial-connected Rewards accounts.

 

The Auto-contribute feature was removed in the 1.75x release.

How do I switch to a different custodial account provider for Brave Rewards?

Once you connect a custodial account—for example, an Uphold, Gemini, or bitFlyer account—to your Brave Rewards profile, you won’t be able to switch to another provider on that profile. However, you can always start a new Brave Rewards profile, then connect your new Brave Rewards profile to an account from a different custodial account provider.

You can create a new Brave Rewards profile by resetting Brave Rewards. You can reset Brave Rewards by going to brave://rewards, then pressing “Reset”. Learn more about resetting Rewards, here.

How many Brave Rewards profiles can be connected to a payout account?

Each payout account can only be linked to a limited number of Brave Rewards profiles. If you see the error message “Limit reached on payout account”, you’ll need to select a different payout account to proceed.

For custodial account providers (such as Uphold, ZebPay, etc.), please note that they typically allow only one account per user. If you believe you’ve reached the Brave Rewards profile limit on your custodial account for a valid reason, please contact support for assistance.

If you’ve reached the limit on a self-custody payout account (e.g., Solana), you’ll need to choose a different account. If you don’t already have another self-custody account, you can create a new Solana account or address using your preferred Solana wallet (such as Brave Wallet).

How to disconnect Brave Rewards?

Once you’ve connected a self-custody wallet or custodial account—such as an Uphold, Gemini, bitFlyer, etc. account—to your Brave Rewards profile, you won’t be able to go back to the original non-connected Brave Rewards state on your current Brave Rewards profile. However, you can always reset Brave Rewards and start with a new Brave Rewards profile that isn’t connected to any custodial account. Learn more about resetting Brave Rewards, here.

I disconnected Brave Browser on my custodial account provider’s website. Why is my account still connected to my Brave Rewards profile?

If you log in to your account on your custodial account provider’s website (like Uphold.com, Gemini.com, etc.), you may find a section in your account settings that lists an application called “Brave Browser”. Deleting “Brave Browser” from this list or revoking access does not disconnect or remove the connection between your Brave Rewards profile and your custodial account.

What does deleting or revoking access to the Brave Browser app do?

When you delete or revoke access to the Brave Browser app, the current authorization session your Brave browser has gets expired. You will then see “Logged out” messaging appear in your Brave Rewards interface for custodial-connected accounts.

Being “Logged out” means that the Brave Rewards feature in your browser will be unable to fetch your current BAT balance from your connected account. It also means you will be unable to send BAT contributions with the BAT from your connected account. However, on Brave’s servers, your Brave Rewards profile is still considered connected to your custodial account.

See here for our Privacy Policy.

Resetting Brave Rewards

To reset your Brave Rewards profile, navigate to the Brave Rewards page (brave://rewards), and select the More option, then Disable and reset Rewards.

By resetting Brave Rewards, you will delete your current Brave Rewards profile and all its data, and Brave Rewards will no longer be enabled. If you enable Brave Rewards again, you will start with an entirely new profile. Data that’ll be reset include things like:

  1. Your Contributions and Monthly Contributions
  2. Your 30-day Ads Viewed and Ads received this month history
  3. Any other settings, preferences, or toggles you may have set to customize your Brave Rewards experience (such as your Brave Rewards country or region setting,ad frequency settings, etc).

⚠️ Will I lose my BAT balance or upcoming earnings by resetting?

  • ✅ BAT balances are saved. Your BAT is actually stored in your connected account (Uphold, Gemini, bitFlyer, ZebPay, or Solana account). Therefore, resetting your Brave Rewards profile will not affect your BAT balance. You can always connect the same account or address to a new profile, and will see your BAT balance reappear in Brave Rewards. 

  • ✅ Ads viewed will be paid. Even if you reset, your earnings from Ads viewed on your previous profile, up approximately to the time you reset, will still be deposited to your account in the next payout period.

Pro tips

  • Before your reset Brave Rewards, you can always go into brave://rewards-internals and copy down the information in the “General info” tab. This may help Brave Support assist you, as it will allow Brave Support to reference your previous Brave Rewards profile. 

  • Many issues can be resolved without resetting your Brave Rewards profile. If you’re not sure, please ask on our official Brave Community support forum.

What does it mean when my Brave Rewards profile is “flagged”?

Sometimes your Brave Rewards profile can be “flagged”. That usually means our automated systems noticed some irregular activity associated with Brave Ads. “Irregular activity” is activity that would be considered unusual compared to an ordinary person using Brave Ads as part of their overall, everyday browsing experience.

Does that mean I did anything wrong?

Not necessarily! Like any automated system, Brave’s flagging system can sometimes make mistakes and produce false positives. 

What happens when I am flagged?

While you are flagged, some Brave Rewards functionality may be disabled or limited. For example, if you are flagged:

  • You will not be able to earn from Brave Ads and will not receive payouts. (Brave Ads may continue to be visible even if your profile is flagged.) 

How do I get unflagged?

As we make changes and improve our automated flagging systems, some previously flagged Rewards profiles will be reevaluated to determine whether their flags can be removed. You can also submit a request to us here.

 

You can also refer to our Brave Rewards: User Terms of Service and general Brave Terms of Use for more information.

Brave Rewards: Connected Accounts with Brave Rewards

Associated Token Accounts (ATAs) on Solana: Receiving BAT on Solana

If you want to receive your earnings from Brave Rewards via Solana, you’ll need to connect a Solana address that has an Associated Token Account (ATA) for Basic Attention Token (BAT). This might sound technical, but don’t worry! In this article, we’ll break down what an ATA is and why you need one to receive your BAT.

What Is an Associated Token Account (ATA)?

An Associated Token Account (ATA) is a special type of account on Solana that is created to hold a specific token (like BAT) for a specific Solana address (your wallet). Think of your Solana address as a “master account” or your main wallet. An ATA is like a sub-account tied to your master account, created specifically to store a particular token.

Why Do You Need an ATA for Brave Rewards?

When Brave sends your BAT rewards to your Solana address, it doesn’t send them directly to your main wallet address. Instead, it sends them to the ATA associated with your address for the BAT token on Solana. Specifically, your BAT earnings are sent directly on-chain to your Solana address in Wormhole-bridged SPL-BAT (This is BAT that was bridged over from the Ethereum network onto Solana via the Wormhole bridge.)

If you don’t have an ATA for BAT, the transaction can’t be completed because there’s no designated place to store the tokens. Creating an ATA is like setting up a labeled inbox for a specific type of mail. Without it, the delivery (your BAT rewards) can’t be properly received and stored.

How do I create an ATA?

When connecting your Solana address to Brave Rewards, we check to see if you already have an ATA for BAT. If not, then you will be prompted to create one. It’s really easy, and your favorite Solana wallet will guide you through the steps, just like any other transaction. Note that it will cost a small amount of SOL to open an ATA, so make sure you have some SOL at your address.

Note that if you have already interacted with Wormhole-bridged  SPL-BAT, then you probably already have an ATA. Just make sure you choose the right Solana address.

What happens if I do not have an ATA?

If you do not have an ATA for Wormhole-bridged SPL-BAT on Solana (for example, if your ATA is closed or has not been created), you will not be eligible to receive Brave Rewards payouts via Solana. Any payouts missed due to not having an ATA for BAT will be considered forfeited. You will not be entitled to recover these missed payouts, even if an ATA is created or re-established at a later time.

Brave Rewards country does not match custodial account country error

When connecting a custodial account (e.g., Uphold, Gemini, bitFlyer, or ZebPay account) to your Brave Rewards profile, your custodial account’s country should match your Brave Rewards country. For example, if your Brave Rewards country is set to the United States (US) but the custodial account you’re using is registered in Brazil (BR), you might not be able to connect your custodial account, and might see the following error message:

Custodial account country

In general, your custodial account country is determined by the ID documents you used during ID verification when signing up with your custodian of choice. For example:

  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from the United States when registering with Uphold, then your custodial account country will be “United States” (US).
  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from Canada, then your custodial account’s country will be Canada (CA).

See our Privacy Policy.

Brave Rewards country

In order to use Brave Rewards, users are prompted to select their country (see screenshot):

The country you select will determine your Brave Rewards country. You can also check your Brave Rewards country by going to brave://rewards-internals and looking at the country code where it says “Rewards country: XX”. 

How do I change my Brave Rewards country?

Currently, the Brave Rewards country you set is permanent. In order to change your Brave Rewards country, you can reset your Brave Rewards profile, then select a different country on your new Rewards profile.

Note: If you’re unable to reset for some reason, please reach out to support for help. 

Having problems?

If you believe that your Brave Rewards country matches your custodial account’s country, but you’re still seeing this error, please reach out to support for help.

Does Brave share data with custodial partners? What does connecting my Brave Rewards profile to a custodial account provider mean for my data?

Brave does not sell users’ personal data: not to advertisers, nor to anyone else. 

Brave operates on the basis of minimizing data flows and storage as a core principle. We go to extreme lengths to ensure we keep only the absolute minimum of user data on our servers, and we share no data except when required to fulfill express user intent.

When you choose to connect a custodial account to your Brave Rewards profile, we receive some data from your chosen custodial account provider. Brave’s use of this data, including what kind of information we receive from the custodial partner as part of your connecting a custodial account to Brave Rewards, is detailed in our Privacy Policy.

Remember: You can use Brave without ever enabling the Brave Rewards feature, and you can use Brave Rewards without ever connecting to one of Brave’s custodial account provider partners.

Sending contributions

When you make an on-demand contribution to a Brave verified creator using BAT from your linked custodial account, your custodian can see and record the details of your contribution transactions (such as, but not limited to, the amount and the recipient). This is subject to the privacy policies of your account provider.

We never collect your browsing history or similar information, and we can’t derive this information from your contributions to content creators or sites.

Gemini account support in Brave Rewards

Gemini payout accounts are no longer supported in Brave Rewards. If you have a Gemini account connected, you’ll need to switch to a different payout method to continue earning BAT and receiving payouts. Other functionality, like sending contributions to creators from your Gemini account via Brave Rewards, will also be unavailable, so we recommend making the switch as soon as you can.

Here’s what to do:

  1. Reset Brave Rewards
  2. Connect a new payout account

We recommend connecting a self-custody wallet for complete control over your BAT.

Don’t worry: Any BAT already in your Gemini account will stay there. Resetting Brave Rewards will allow you to connect a new payout account.

If you have any other questions, you can submit a support ticket, or join us on our community forums.

How is the country of my custodial account determined?

In general, your account country is determined by the country of the ID documents you used during ID verification with your selected account provider. For example:

  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from the United States when registering with Uphold, then your custodial account country will be “United States” (US).
  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from Canada, then your custodial account’s country will be Canada (CA).

You can see our Privacy Policy here.

New signups for Brave Rewards are currently disabled in your region

Brave Rewards can sometimes be unavailable for new signups in certain regions. This is usually temporary, and signups will be restored once the program is ready to accept new users again in your region. 

If you are seeing this message and would like to join Brave Rewards, we recommend trying again every so often. 

Unavailable jurisdictions

A small number of regions are disabled on a more permanent basis. You can find a list of unavailable jurisdictions here.

What is “KYC” and how does it fit into Brave Rewards?

KYC (“Know Your Customer”) is the process by which a business identifies and verifies a customer’s identity. By law, KYC is required of certain businesses—such as banks, financial services, exchanges, custodial account services, etc.—in order to comply with anti-money laundering (AML) regulations.

For example, in order to connect a custodial account to your Brave Rewards profile, your custodial account needs to have completed KYC (ID-verification).  

What is a “custodian” or “custodial account provider”? A custodian is a company that holds your BAT for you. This includes crypto exchanges like Gemini or bitFlyer, and services like Uphold. 

💡You can also connect your Brave Rewards to a self-custody account, like Brave Wallet. There is no third-party or custodian holding your assets for you with this option.

Why do I need to KYC?

KYC or ID-verification is required to enable and use Brave Rewards if connecting with a custodian. A user must complete KYC verification to access the following:

  • Earning/Accruing: To begin earning and accruing BAT for Brave Ads, you will need to connect a custodial account.
  • Withdrawals: If the user would like to withdraw BAT from the platform (e.g., to an external Ethereum address or a service that permits such a function, including exchanging BAT).
  • Deposits of external BAT: If the user would like to deposit additional BAT to be used inside the Brave Rewards ecosystem (for example, depositing externally-sourced BAT to tip to creators in the Brave Rewards ecosystem)

Doesn’t forcing KYC go against Brave’s stance on privacy?

Please note that users do not undergo KYC or ID-verification with Brave, but with their selected custodial account provider. Since Brave does not perform KYC or ID-verification, Brave never has access to your ID documents, etc. You can read our Privacy Policy, which outlines the information we receive from our custodial partners. 

Note: You can also connect your Brave Rewards to a self-custody account, like Brave Wallet. There is no third-party or custodian involved with this option.

What is a connected Brave Rewards profile? How do I connect an account to my Brave Rewards profile?

A “connected Brave Rewards profile” means that you’ve connected a custodial account or self-custody wallet to your Brave Rewards profile.

What is a “custodial account”? A custodial account is an account with a company—a custodian—that holds your BAT for you. This includes crypto exchanges like Gemini or bitFlyer, and services like Uphold. 

A self-custodyaccount, like Brave Wallet, means you alone have the ability to manage (or transact with) your assets, like BAT. There is no third-party or intermediary holding your assets for you.

What happens when I connect a custodial account?

When you connect a custodial account:

  1. Earning and Accruing BAT Rewards: You will begin earning and accruing BAT for Brave Ads you see, as part of Brave Rewards.

  2. Your Brave Rewards BAT balance is read from your account. The BAT balance you see in the Brave Rewards interface is a reflection of BAT you have inside your custodial account. 

  3. You can add externally-purchased BAT to be used in Brave Rewards. Since your BAT balance is connected to your custodial account, you can purchase BAT elsewhere, deposit it into your custodial account, then have access to that BAT in Brave Rewards. You can use your externally-purchased BAT to contribute to your favorite Brave creators, for example.

List of custodial partners

Brave is currently partnered with three different custodial account providers:

  • Gemini 
  • Uphold
  • bitFlyer (Japan only)
  • ZebPay (India only)

Support for verifying your Brave Rewards profile varies by custodian and region. You can find a list of supported regions for each custodian in this support article.

Notes

In the past, being “connected” used to be called “verified”.

What is the difference between self-custody and custodial linking?

You can connect a Brave Rewards profile through a self-custody wallet or custodial account.

A self-custodyaccount, like Brave Wallet, means you alone have the ability to manage (or transact with) your assets, like BAT. There is no third-party or intermediary holding your assets for you.

A custodialaccount is an account with a company or third-party (custodian) that holds your BAT for you. This includes crypto exchanges like Uphold or ZebPay. The list of supported regions for custodial accounts can be found here.

Brave Rewards: Creators & Contributions

Brave Creator FAQ

Below is a list of commonly asked questions related to issues being a creator with Brave Creators. If you still need assistance please reach out to the team here.

 

What is Brave Creators?

Brave Creators allows you to receive contributions from your fans and supporters. Register your website or social media accounts to begin receiving payouts and direct, onchain contributions. 

How do Brave users contribute to Creators?

Users can contribute to Brave Creators through:

  1. On-Demand Contributions: A one-time contribution in the form of BAT, USDC, ETH or Solana.
  2. Recurring Contributions: A monthly contribution in the form of BAT. It will recur every 30 days.

You can learn more about contributions here.

Do I need a custodial account to receive contributions?

No, you do not need a custodial account to receive tips and contributions.

To become a “verified creator” and display the blue checkmark to Brave users, you can:

  1. Connect a Self-Custody Crypto Address: Link a Solana or Ethereum crypto address to your individual sites or channels.

  2. Connect a Custodial Account: Connect an Uphold, Gemini, or bitFlyer account to your Brave Creators account. (See here for a list of supported regions.)

Why is my site or channel not showing as “verified”?

This can occur if your site or channel does not have a connected account/address. You can connect a custodial account, a crypto address, or both. 

What should I do if I am unable to login to my Creator account or lose my 2FA credentials?

Please visit this article to reset your 2FA. Note, that there is a waiting period between resets. 

If you are unable to receive a login email, check your spam/junk folder. Please reach out to us here if you continue to have login trouble.

Creators: Custom URLs for Contribution Pages

In Brave Creators, you can choose your own custom URL for your shareable contribution page. Please keep the following guidelines in mind:

Requirements and Restrictions

  • Length: Your custom URL must be between 3 and 32 characters long.
  • Allowed Characters: Only letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), underscores (_), and hyphens (-) are permitted.
  • Case-Insensitivity: Custom URLs are case-insensitive. For example, Example and example will be treated as the same URL.
  • Change Frequency: You can only change your custom URL once every 60 days.
  • Availability: If you change your custom URL or delete your account, your previous custom URL will remain unavailable for a period of time before it can be reused.

Brave reserves the right to revoke any custom URL for any reason, especially if it violates our policies or is deemed inappropriate. We may also render a custom URL permanently unavailable at any time and for any reason.

Reporting Inappropriate URLs

If you encounter an inappropriate URL, please report it to Brave using the following support form: https://support.brave.com/hc/en-us/requests/new

Disclaimer

Please note that these rules are subject to change. By using the custom URLs feature, you acknowledge and understand the above guidelines.

How do I connect an Ethereum or Solana address to my channel?

To get started, select Add Channel in your Brave Creators dashboard. Select the type of channel you’d like to add.

 

Next, you’ll see the option to connect your address for the desired channel. You can choose Ethereum, Solana, or both.

 

Select Add new address. 

 

Brave Wallet will prompt you to choose and connect your desired address. Please check the default wallet settings if you do not see your desired wallet provider appear. 

 

Your signature will be requested to verify ownership.

 

Once connected, the Appear as Verified status will appear in the top-right of your site or channel.

Your Brave Creators channel can receive direct, onchain contributions from supporters and fans. You can learn more about on-demand contributions here.

How do I connect my Creators account with a custodian?

You can connect your Brave Creators account with a self-custody wallet and/or a custodial account. Instructions for connecting a Web3 address can be found here.

A custodial account is an account with a company or third-party (custodian) that holds your BAT for you. This includes crypto exchanges like Uphold. This list of supported regions for custodial accounts can be found here.

Verifying your custodial account means performing ID-verification (or “KYC”) for your account. Please note, the verification process is independent of Brave and handled by the custodian.

To connect your custodian account

Visit your Brave Creators dashboard and Select your region.

Once your region is selected you will be presented with the option to connect an available custodian.

The custodian verification may not process immediately. Please reach out to Uphold Support for any issues with your Uphold account. If you do not see an available custodian please check your region. This list of supported regions for custodial accounts can be found here.

Monthly recurring contributions are only available for custodian-connected accounts. You can learn more here.

How do I register or add my sites/channels to my Brave Creators account?

To get started, select “Add Channel” in your Brave Creators dashboard. You’ll then be prompted to choose the type of channel (Websites, YouTube/Twitch channels, etc.) you’d like to add.

If you’re adding a channel (such as a YouTube or Vimeo channel) or a social media account (like an X/Twitter or Reddit account), you’ll be able to register your channel or account with Brave Creators by just signing in with your account on the relevant platform.

If you’re adding a website, you can prove ownership of your website and its domain name with the following methods: 

File Upload Verification

This is the simplest and easiest method for most users. It requires:

  • An HTTPS enabled website
  • Access to your website’s hosting account

This method involves adding a .txt file to a specific folder (.well_known) within your website’s hosting. After you have verified with this method, you can remove the .txt file from your hosting. Rewards will prompt you to download this file during the verification process. It must be named “brave-rewards-verification.txt”.

The token text looks something like this:

brave-ledger-verification=0e5e9be6d9a40ff3da74315f3ba41383a3a5f9ec0a83c2040b78eb77543ab3582721ea

DNS Verification

DNS verification is a good fallback if you have problems with file upload verification or don’t have access to your hosting account. It requires:

  • Access to your domain host

You will have to add a DNS TXT record to your site’s domain. The content of this TXT record should be the Brave verification token text. Rewards will supply this during the verification process.

After being verified, you can remove the DNS verification record.

IMPORTANT: Note that subdomains cannot be separately verified unless they are part of the public suffix list. Otherwise, verifications for subdomains will point toward the primary domain. For example, “hello.example.com” will actually be “example.com”.

How do I set up 2-Factor Authentication for Brave Creators?

You can enable 2-Factor Authentication (2FA) on your Creators account by navigating to the Security settings. This allows you to scan a QR code or use a numerical code to link your Creators account to a 2FA app that generates login codes. We recommend Authy for this purpose. Other 2FA apps are available on the Google Play Store and the Apple App store.

WARNING: Make sure to keep a backup of your 2FA codes. If you lose access to your 2-factor authentication method (such as a lost device) you will be unable to login to your Creators account and will have to create a new account and transfer your old channels over to it.

How to become a Verified Creator with Brave Creators

Last updated: May 12, 2025

What is a verified creator?

A verified creator is someone who can receive tips and contributions in BAT (Basic Attention Token) from Brave Rewards users who visit their registered websites and channels. Creators eligible for contributions are marked with a special blue check mark in the URL bar, indicating their connected status.

To become a “verified creator” and display the blue checkmark to Brave users, you need to:

  1. Connect a Custodial Account: Connect an Uphold, Gemini, or bitFlyer account to your Brave Creators account. (See here for a list of supported regions.)

  2. Connect a Self-Custody Crypto Address: Link a Solana or Ethereum crypto address to your individual sites or channels.

Connecting a custodial account

Support for connecting a custodial account to your Brave Creators account varies by account provider and region. You can find the list of supported countries for each custodial account provider here.

Accounts from unsupported regions

You can still link a custodial account to your Brave Creators account even if your region is not supported. However, your registered sites/channels won’t appear as verified until your region is supported. Once it is, your channels will then automatically show the verified status, saving you from needing to constantly check for updates.

Determining your custodial account country

The country for your custodial account is based on the ID documents you used during ID verification/KYC with your account provider. For example:

  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from the United States when registering with Uphold, then your custodial account country will be “United States” (US).
  • If you used a driver’s license or passport from Canada, then your custodial account’s country will be Canada (CA).

Connecting crypto addresses

Beside each of your sites/channels, you will see an option to connect a crypto address (Ethereum or Solana). Brave users who visit your sites/channels with crypto addresses connected will see you as a “verified creator” with a blue checkmark.

Managing your Creators Account

You can manage various settings on your Creators account such as account deletion, email subscription, and contact information from the Account Settings page. 

How to Delete Your Brave Creators Account

You can delete your Brave Creators account and any related data at any time via the Creators dashboard. 

To delete your account, follow these steps:

  1. Login to creators.brave.com

  2. Click the Settings tab on the left-side of the screen. This will take you to the Account Settings page.

  3. Under the “Account Deletion” section, select the “Delete My Account” button.

  4. You will be asked to confirm the process. Keep in mind that any pending BAT balances tied to your Creators account will be permanently lost if you decide to delete your account.

  5. If there is unsettled BAT, your email will be mapped to that account for a year. If there is no BAT to settle, all of your account information will be deleted immediately.

How to Change your Subscription Settings for Brave/BAT Marketing Emails

When signing up for Creators, you can decide whether to opt-in to Brave marketing emails. If you change your mind later, you can adjust these settings from the Account Settings screen when logged into Creators by ticking or unticking the box here:

An Important Note on Transactional Emails

We, at Brave, have the obligation to inform you about changes to your account and information about changes to Brave’s terms of services and other notifications. The only way to opt out of this information is to delete your account.

How to Change your Contact Information

Lastly, you can also change the name and email address tied to your Creators account from the Account Settings page. Make sure you’re logged in, and click “Edit Contact” under the Contact section. Click “Save” when you are finished.

What do I do if I get locked out of my account?

Resetting your Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

If you have lost your 2nd factor authentication, you may choose to use the Two-Factor Removal feature on the Brave Creators web app. To do this:

  1. Attempt to log into your creators account as you normally would.
  2. Click theWe can help button at the bottom of the screen.
  3. Click the purple Request 2-factor Security Removal button.

     

You’ll be redirected to the 2FA “wait” screen where you can see the remaining time left on your 2FA reset.

Please note that for your security, the 2FA removal process will require a 2-day waiting period. Additionally, once your 2-factor authentication is removed:

  • The account channels will need to be re-verified. 
  • The account wallet will need to be re-added. 
  • There will be a 30 day waiting period before reconnecting.

If you wish to cancel your 2FA removal request, you may do so from the wait screen. A cancellation request will be sent to your e-mail address.

Re-verifying your channels under a new account

You may also transfer your channels to a new Rewards account if you’re unable to login to your current account. To Create a new account:

  1. Under a new email address, at creators.brave.com
  2. Verify your old channels via the Creator’s dashboard. You can view a tutorial on channel verification here. 
  3. Once your channels are verified on your new account, they will transfer from your old account to your new account within 10 days. You will get a confirmation email that also allows you to cancel the channel transfer if it was done in error.

Note: Your BAT Creator balance (as well as referral statistics, etc.) will transfer to your new account. No BAT will be lost due to channel transfers.

Brave Rewards: Getting Started with BAT & Rewards

Brave Rewards FAQ

What is “Brave Rewards”?

Brave Rewards is a program that lets you earn tokens that you can use to redeem rewards or support the sites you visit. Brave Rewards is composed of a few different features: Brave Ads and Contributions.

Brave Ads allows you to earn Basic Attention Tokens (or “BAT”) for seeing privately-matched ads that you can control. On-Demand Contributions allow you to make on-demand tips to websites and content creators, such as your favorite YouTube channels, Twitter users, Twitch streamers, and more.

Do I have to participate in Rewards in order to use Brave?

You do not need to participate in Rewards in order to enjoy Brave. However, note that sponsored images on the New Tab Page are on by default, but can easily be disabled. (If you enable Brave Rewards, you will earn for the New Tab Page sponsored images you see.)

How do I setup Brave Rewards?

To begin earning for seeing Brave Ads, you’ll need to connect an account from one of our custodial partners or with your self-custody wallet. This will give us a place to send you your BAT earnings each month.  Once you connect an account, you’ll unlock the full Brave Rewards experience. For example, in addition to earning for Brave Ads, you’ll also be able to send contributions to websites and creators.

What’s the difference between On-Demand Contributions and Recurring Contributions?

On-Demand contributions can be done at any time. You can make one time contributions to sites or channels.

To automatically send a contribution of some amount every month to a creator, toggle on the “recurring contribution” option when making an on-demand contribution. Your contribution will recur every 30 days automatically. 

Do I have to use one or the other? Can I use both?

Users decide what works for them. You may use one, both, or neither of these features in Brave. 

On-Demand contributions must be set up manually by nature, so users who don’t wish to tip don’t need to interact with this functionality.

Please note, recurring contributions are only available for custodial-connected Rewards accounts.

What exactly is a “verified” site?

A verified website/channel is one that has registered with the Brave Rewards program for Creators, allowing it to receive BAT contributions from Brave users.

Note: A site’s verification status does not represent a business partnership or endorsement by Brave Software.

How can I tell if a site or channel is verified?

In the contribution panel, verified websites are marked with a blue checkmark, and will show text that reads “Verified Creator”. The contribution panel can be accessed by pressing the BAT logo in the URL bar.

Will Brave sell user data to advertisers?

Brave does not collect personal user data, and would never sell any data to advertisers. With Brave Ads, ads presented are based on your interests, as inferred from your local browsing behavior. No personal data or browsing history ever leaves your browser. 

Does Brave Rewards work in every country?

Due to regulations, some countries are not eligible to participate in Brave Rewards. See our article on restricted jurisdictions.

How do I connect Brave Rewards to a self-custody wallet?

Prerequisites

To begin earning with Brave Ads via Solana you’ll need a self-custody wallet, like Brave Wallet, and a small amount of the Solana token. If you already have a Solana wallet and SOL, you can move on to the next step. 

  1. Self-custody wallet: You must have a Brave Wallet or another wallet that supports Solana. You can learn how to setup a Brave Wallet here: Creating your Brave Wallet

  2. Solana token: A small amount of SOL is required to create the Associated Token Account (ATA) for Basic Attention Token (BAT). This is a special type of account on Solana that is created to hold BAT on your Solana address. You can learn more about the requirement here. 

    You can add SOL to your wallet a few different ways:

    • Purchasing through an on-ramp provider. 
    • Depositing or sending Solana from another wallet or exchange.
    • Bridging funds to Solana from another chain or network. 

Connecting to Solana

Navigate to the Rewards icon in your address bar and click Connect account. Enable Brave Rewards if you haven’t already.

 

The options to choose between a custodial and self-custody account will appear. Select Brave Wallet. 

 

Choose your desired Solana wallet to connect. 

 

A list of your available Solana addresses will appear in Brave Wallet. Choose the address you wish to connect with Rewards and click Next. 

 

Review the permission duration and select Connect.

 

Next, you will be prompted to Create BAT account. 

Note: You must have SOL on your connected address to proceed. You can learn more about the requirement here.

 

Brave Wallet will prompt you to review the transaction. Click Confirm to approve the transaction and create your BAT account.

 

Congrats! Your Solana address is now connected. You can manage your Rewards account at brave://rewards.

How do I setup Brave Rewards?

To begin earning for seeing Brave Ads, you’ll need to connect an account from one of our custodial partners or with your self-custody wallet. This will give us a place to send you your BAT earnings each month. 

  • Desktop
  • Android
  • iOS

Desktop

To enable Brave Rewards click on the Rewards icon in your URL bar.

Select your region.

Connect an account to start earning.

Use the Rewards settings page (brave://rewards) to fine-tune your Brave Rewards settings. 

Android

To enable Brave Rewards click on the Rewards icon in your URL bar. Alternatively, Click on the Menu (⋮) > Brave Rewards.

Select your region.

Connect an account to start earning.

Use the Rewards settings page (brave://rewards) to fine-tune your Brave Rewards settings. 

 

iOS

There is limited functionality on iOS. Learn more.

How do I view my BAT balance and history on Solana?

To view the BAT history for your Solana-connected account, navigate to your Rewards panel and find the Payout account section. 

Click the drop-down arrow and select Go to my account.

You will be redirected to the Solana Explorer. Here you can view details like token balances and transaction history.

In the Overview section, you will see the wallet address connected to your Rewards account and the Solana (SOL) balance. When an Account does not exist, it means the address has not been funded with Solana. The Solana (SOL) token is required to send your deposited BAT.

 

The Token Holdings section will display the Total BAT currently held on this account address.

 

In the Token History section you can view the transaction history for all tokens. Filter by BAT - Basic Attention to view the potential Brave Rewards deposits only. Click on the transaction signature link to view the specific transaction details.

 

After clicking on the transaction signature link above, you will see the Timestamp for the BAT deposit.

 

Scroll further down the page to view the Token Balances section. This will show you the total amount sent and deposited for this transaction. 

 

You can learn more about SPL-BAT here.

How to transfer SPL-BAT?

Solana (SOL) is required to pay the fee associated with sending and transacting on the Solana network. If you are receiving a message related to Insufficient Funds you will need to add Solana to the same wallet address as your SPL-BAT address. You can do so by depositing SOL into your wallet address or purchasing directly through one of our on-ramp providers.

How to transfer SPL-BAT:

  1. In Brave, click the icon in the browser toolbar.
  2. Enter your password to unlock your secure wallet.
  3. Select send in the wallet panel.

The below screen will appear in your wallet. Choose the Select token option.

Find the Basic Attention Token (Portal) option. Search for it if not visible.

Select the amount you wish to send and enter the address of the recipient.

Confirm the address and recipient. 

Once ready, double check the address one last time and review the transaction fees. If everything looks correct, confirm the transaction to post it to the blockchain and initiate the transfer.

What is BAT and SPL-BAT?

Basic Attention Token (BAT) is an ERC-20 token, native to the Ethereum blockchain, and can be stored in ERC-20 compatible wallets. We’ve also bridged BAT onto the Solana network, making it an SPL token that users can leverage in the Solana ecosystem and with SPL compatible wallets. 

Brave Rewards on Solana utilizes SPL-BAT, bridged from Ethereum to Solana via the Wormhole bridge. Click here to learn more about the Basic Attention Token.

Brave Sync: Sync basics

Delete Sync Account FAQ

Should you ever want to delete your Sync account for any reason, you can do this from any device that is a part of the Sync chain. To do this:

  1. Launch Brave and go to Settings –> Managed Synced Devices (on mobile it will be Settings –> Sync)
  2. Scroll down to the bottom of the page
  3. Click Delete Sync Account

What is the “Delete Sync account” feature?

This feature allows Brave users to delete their previously-synced data from Brave servers.

Can I create a new Sync chain after I delete the old one?

Yes, you will still be able to user Brave Sync by creating a new chain once your current chain is deleted.

What will happen if I have synced across different versions of the Brave Browser? Is it possible to delete the chain in this case?

Yes. If you use the “Delete Sync account” feature in the latest version of Brave, all devices will lose access to the Sync account and the encrypted data will be permanently removed from the server. This happens regardless of which version of Brave is running on the other devices in the chain.

Will synced data such as bookmarks, history, and passwords be removed from local device storage after the Sync chain has been deleted?

No. The data which was previously synced remains on each device. It just won’t be synced to other devices or to Brave’s servers.

Can I recover my Sync account after I delete it?

No - you cannot recover your Sync chain once it has been deleted. This deletion is permanent and you will need to create a new Sync chain and have one of your devices re-upload the data.

How do I set up Sync?

Note: This article only covers how to setup Brave Sync on your devices. Please see our other articles on Sync for more detailed information on Sync and Sync behavior:

  • Sync FAQ
  • Understanding Brave Sync

Important: Only enable Sync on devices you own or control access to.

💡Note: At this time, we are currently leveraging use of a 25th Sync code word to Sync a new device to the chain. If you are using the code words (as opposed to scanning the QR code) to Sync a new device, please enter your 24 word code, then enter the rotating 25th Sync code word that can be found here in order to add your new device to the Sync chain.

Create Sync Chain (Desktop)

When a Sync “chain” is created, any device that is on that chain will be synchronized and share the same data, such as bookmarks, open tabs, browsing history and more.  To start using Brave Sync:

  1. Select Menu `` → Brave Sync.

  2. Select Start a new sync chain.

  3. Choose your other mobile device (Phone/Tablet) or Computer to begin the Sync chain.

Sync Your Data - Desktop to Mobile

When Syncing your desktop browser with mobile devices, you will be presented with a Sync Code in the form of a QR code that you can scan with your mobile device camera to begin the Sync chain. You may also enter the Sync code manually. 

  1. Open Brave Browser on your mobile device and go to Settings → Sync.
  2. Select Scan or enter your sync code.
  3. Once you scan the Sync Code, please wait as we connect your devices via Sync Chain. Select ‘OK’ or the ‘X’ close button. You will be taken back to the main Brave Sync page with your devices in the sync chain listed.

Sync Your Data - Desktop to Desktop

If selecting another desktop computer, you will be presented with a 24 word “Sync Code”. Enter this code into your second computer to add it to the Sync chain. This 24 word code is unique to your Sync Chain, please keep it private.

  1. Enter the word code into your second computer to begin the Sync Chain.
  2. Go to your other Computer and select Menu → Brave Sync.
  3. In your second computer, this time select Enter a sync chain code.
  4. Enter your Sync Chain code in to your second computer.

Once you enter the Sync Chain Code, please wait as we connect your devices via Sync Chain. Select ok or the ‘X’ close button. You will be taken back to the main Brave Sync page with your devices in the sync chain listed:

Brave Sync now allows you to sync multiple different data types across your devices (where applicable). When Sync runs, any of the available items toggled “on” will be synchronized across devices. If a datatype is toggled “off”, that device will not send or receive updates for that data. Syncable data includes:

  • Bookmarks
  • Passwords
  • Autofill Data
  • History
  • Open Tabs
  • Extensions
  • Themes
  • Apps  

Sync Data from your Mobile Device

  • Android
  • iOS
Sync Android Data

To start a Sync Chain from Brave Browser on your Android Device:

  1. Open the Main menu, go to Settings → Sync in the Advanced section.
  2. Select Start a new sync chain to add a new mobile device or a computer to the newly created Chain. You will be presented with a QR code to scan if you are adding a mobile device, or a word code if adding a computer.

   

  1. Once you enter the Sync Chain Code, please wait as we connect your devices via Sync Chain.

Select ‘OK’ or the ‘X’ close button. You will be returned to the main Brave Sync page with your devices in the sync chain listed.

On the main Sync page, you should see the Categories, Add another device, and Remove this device options:

  • Add another device allows you to add another mobile or desktop device to the Sync chain and you can use.
  • Remove this device allows you to remove the device in use from the active Sync chain. 
  • Categories allows you to select individual data types to be Synced.

   

iOS

Note: At this time, iOS Sync only Syncs bookmark data. We are working to include all data types in Sync as soon as possible.

To start a Sync Chain from Brave Browser on your iOS device:

  1. Open the Menu, go to Settings → Other Settings → Sync.

  2. Select Start a new Sync Chain to add a new mobile device or computer to the newly created Chain.

  3. You will be shown a QR code to scan when adding mobile devices, or a word code when adding a computer.

  4. Once you enter the Sync Chain Code, please wait as we connect your devices via Sync Chain. Select ‘OK’ or the ‘X’ close button. You will be returned to the main Brave Sync page with your devices in the sync chain listed.

Data Syncing

As you add, remove or make changes to your data on devices that are on the same Sync chain, these changes will be reflected across all other devices on that same chain when a Sync update is called. This process happens automatically and at regular (frequent) intervals.

Note that users who have a lot of browsing data (ex. 1000+ bookmarks) may experience a short delay before new data is displayed properly. Please be patient as it can sometimes take a moment to Sync large amounts of data in this way.

To Reset your Sync Chain

Select the Leave Sync Chain button at the bottom of the page:

Removing a device from the Sync chain will stop any data from syncing to or from that device. Your local data will be retained but all the data in the Brave’s Sync cache will be deleted.

To Delete Sync Chain

Selecting the Delete Sync account at the bottom of the page will remove all devices from the chain and delete any data on the server itself.

Note that this action cannot be undone. See our FAQ here for more information on the Delete Sync account option.

Sync FAQ

Why am I seeing the “Brave was unable to access your system’s secure storage…” error message?

As it’s name suggests, this error will appear when Brave Sync is trying to access your safe storage data, when it doesn’t have the proper access to. This typically happens when system login credentials are changed, permissions are changed or sometimes after a system update.

For users on macOS:

Users on macOS seeing this error message should see a notification prompting you to enter your password to the keychain, as shown below, granting safe storage access to the browser:

If you do not see this prompt but are still seeing the error, you can still grant access manually by:

  1. Open theKeychain Access app

  2. Choose Login under theDefault keychains section on the left

  3. FindBrave Safe Storage

  4. Click onAccess control and check to see if Brave Browser is listed here:

    If it is not, click the+button and add it, thenSave changes(you’ll have to re-enter your password).

For Linux users encountering this

As with macOS, Linux uses should see a similar prompt:

If not, you can manually grant access by:

  1. Open thePasswords and Keysapp
  2. Ensure that the icon is unlocked (clickUnlockand enter your password to unlock)
  3. Check to see ifBrave Safe Storage is there — if not, please click the+button to add it.

For Windows users encountering this

Unfortunately there is no quick fix for this on Windows — again, this typically only happens when you make changes to your system user name/password credentials. Typically, only a user with the same logon credential as the user who encrypted the data can decrypt the data. In addition, the encryption and decryption usually must be done on the same computer.

As such, we recommend resetting Sync and re-syncing your devices. You can do this by going tobrave://sync-internalsand using theDisable Sync (Clear data)option.

 

How does Brave Sync v2 differ from Sync v1?

Sync v1 was a completely custom sync system, built as part of the old “Muon” browser.  Sync v1 stored all data into an encrypted log on S3.  New browsers joining the sync chain had to download all the logs and re-assemble the events in order.  The browsers were also responsible for cleaning up out of date data records.

Sync v2 was rebuilt to be more directly compatible with the Chromium sync system (Chromium is the same open source base of Google’s Chrome and Brave).  Brave built a sync server that more directly followed Chromium’s sync protocol, but defaulting instead to use encrypted data records.  Sync v2 more easily supports more sync data types, while still keeping the client side data encrypted, so only you can see your data.

What devices are compatible with Brave Sync?

Brave Sync allows you to synchronize data across any number of Desktop, Android, and iOS devices.

Do I have a Sync “account”?

Unlike in Chrome, there is no Brave “account” that you can sign into. Instead, Brave uses the same “Sync chain” concept as before. Brave also enforces client-side encryption to keep your data safe and secure. Additionally, all Sync data is sent to Brave operated servers (no data is sent to Google or anywhere else). You can read more about how Brave Sync v2 system works here.

I have a Sync key from when Brave first released the feature, will it still work on version 2?

While the Sync chain concept itself is more or less the same, Brave Sync v2 uses a different system entirely. Subsequently, recovery phrases from Sync v1 will not work with v2 – you will have to start a new Sync chain using the new system.

How does my data stay private? How is it encrypted?

We use the built-in custom passphrase feature from Chromium sync and encrypt everything client-side. Instead of letting the user pick a passphrase, which may be weak, we force the passphrase to be the BIP39 encoding of the sync seed. The rest of the encryption is handled by Chromium as follows:

  1. BIP39 phrase is key-stretched using scrypt(N = 2^13, r = 8, p = 11). New clients need the scrypt salt in order to derive the key.
  2. Then the stretched key is used directly as a AES128-CTR-HMAC encryption key.

How long will my Sync data be available on the server?

Your Sync data on the Sync server will be available as long as one of your devices is actively using it. Server data which has not been accessed in 12 months will be permanently deleted. Local copies of the data in your browser will not be affected by this automatic expiration of the server data.

Why can’t I Sync my Rewards data using Brave Sync?

The Brave Sync team first focused on providing all of the popular sync data types that users have come to depend on, e.g. bookmarks, passwords, history, etc. The Brave team is working next on syncing rewards data. More to come soon!

Why don’t I see all of my browsing History Synced between devices?

When History is synced, you are essentially syncing typed URLs entered after both devices are added to the same Sync chain. Let’s say for example you have two devices, both with ~1,000 entries in History. When these two devices are added to the same Sync chain, they will both retain those same 1000 entries – but any newly typed URLs entered into the address bar will now be added to both devices.

Why won’t my data Sync on my Android device?

Sync v2 on Android respects the system-wide option “Automatically sync data”, so if you found that Brave Sync v2 does not work on your Android device, you should ensure that system option is in the position `on`. The location of that option depends on device manufacturer, but you may find it in:

  • System settings --> Accounts --> Automatically Sync Data
  • System settings --> Accounts and backup --> Accounts --> Auto Sync Data
  • System settings --> Cloud and accounts --> Accounts --> Auto Sync Data

In order to sync v2 work on Android it is required to turn that option on.

Sync v1 was a completely custom sync system, built as part of the old “Muon” browser.  Sync v1 stored all data into an encrypted log on S3.  New browsers joining the sync chain had to download all the logs and re-assemble the events in order.  The browsers were also responsible for cleaning up out of date data records. Sync v2 was rebuilt to be more directly compatible with the Chromium sync system (Chromium is the same open source base of Google’s Chrome and Brave).  Brave built a sync server that more directly followed Chromium’s sync protocol, but defaulting instead to use encrypted data records.  Sync v2 more easily supports more sync data types, while still keeping the client side data encrypted, so only you can see your data.

You can read more about how Brave Sync v2 system works here.

Let’s say for example you have two devices, both with ~1,000 entries in History. When these two devices are added to the same Sync chain, they will both retain those same 1000 entries – but any newly typed URLs entered into the address bar will now be added to both devices.

  • System settings -- Accounts -- Automatically Sync Data
  • System settings -- Accounts and backup -- Accounts -- Auto Sync Data

In order to sync v2 work on Android it is required to turn that option on.

Understanding Brave Sync

Note: This is a brief explanation of how Brave Sync should function for users who are unfamiliar with or unclear on what to expect from Sync.

What does it mean to “Sync” my data?

Brave Sync allows you to synchronize your browsing data across all of your devices. This way, you have access to the same bookmarks, browsing history and other data regardless of which device you are using.

It also makes adding or removing data easier by automatically syncing those changes to each device so that you only have to make the change once, instead of making the change on each individual device. For a deeper understanding of the internal Sync mechanism, please see:

  • Help Center Sync FAQ
  • Brave Sync wiki (Github)

Understanding Sync Behavior

When you add devices to a Sync chain, Brave Sync will initiate automatically. When this happens, information from each device will merge. Then, changes in any device will propagate and sync to the other devices and data will be the same across all devices for the synced data types.

You can toggle the type of data you’d like to be synced in Settings → Sync. If a data type is toggled “on”, it will both receive data updated or changed from other devices on the chain, as well as send data updated on the device to other devices on the chain. Observe the examples below:

In the image above, Example 1 shows a Sync chain with three connected devices, configured to Sync all data types. A change is made to Bookmark data (a new bookmark was added) in Device 1, which then propagates to both other devices on the chain. Likewise, if a change in bookmark data on Device 2 (a bookmark is deleted), that change is reflected on Devices 1 and 3.

In the examples above, we considered each device to Sync “all” possible data types. However you may want to only Sync specific data between devices so that only those data are propagated when a change occurs. For example, you may want to only Sync bookmarks and passwords, but no other data between devices. You can do this by disabling the desired data types on a device, after-which that device will not receive that data from, nor will it send that data to other devices on the chain. We show another example of this behavior below:

In Example 3, Device 2 has the Bookmarks data type toggled “off”. Now, when a change in bookmark data is made to another device ( a bookmark was added to device 1), Device 2 does not receive this data and the change is not reflected on the device. Further, example four shows that if a change in bookmark data on Device 2 is made (a bookmark was deleted) the other devices on the chain do not receive it.

Sync vs Import/Export

Syncing data is not the equivalent of importing or exporting data. Importing or exporting data is typically a one-way, isolated event. That is, data is transferred in the state that it’s in from one device/location to another and stops once the transfer is complete. Further changes made to that data on either device are not reflected on the other.

This is inherently different from Sync, since all devices on the chain are synchronized and will have the same state. However, you can “mimic” a data import by Syncing your devices once, then either disabling all syncable data types or simply leaving the Sync chain once data is synchronized.

How do I submit a bug report?

The software development process is often an arduous one. Large scale applications can contain millions of lines of code that need to work across multiple platforms as well as account for a nearly infinite number of possible conditions at runtime. Subsequently, software at this scale is rarely perfect and may not always behave as intended. We generally refer to flaws, errors, or otherwise unintended behavior as bugs.

Brave is a new, innovative, and ambitious project with many moving parts. While our team is extremely talented and driven, you’re likely to encounter bugs sometimes while browsing. You can help us continue to improve our product and deliver a better browsing experience by bringing these bugs you encounter to our attention. 

The best places to submit issues to are:

  • On our Community support website
  • On our official Github page
  • On our Brave browser subreddit

However, the fastest and easiest way is by visiting our Community website and posting the issue you are encountering for our Support and Brave Team staff to see. It also includes the benefit of many Community members and mods who are always willing to help solve your issues as well.

If you are posting on Community, you can follow these guidelines to ensure you receive the best support:

Before posting

As we continue to grow, so do the number of support requests we receive. Before you post to Community, take a moment to do the following:

  • Look through this knowledge base It’s built to address many common questions and known issues. While still a work in progress, content will be regularly added and is always worth checking here first to see if your issue is covered.
  • Look for Duplicates Given the amount of reports/request we get each day, there’s a good chance that someone else may have raised your issue already or may have been resolved. Before posting, use the search bar on the top-right corner of the website to see if other users have raised the same concern.

Using the template

When posting a new topic on Community, you may notice that that the editor comes pre-filled with some information. What you’re seeing is the bug reporting template we’ve inserted to make submitting support requests and reporting issues as simple as possible.

Read the instructions at the top of the template and simply insert your information below the appropriate section. When properly filled the template will ideally tell Brave team members all they need to know about the problem you’re having at a glance and eliminates unnecessary back and fourth responses used to discern some basic information needed to diagnose an issue. Additionally, the title of your post should be succinct and informative.

When filled out properly, your report should look something like this:

Description of the issue: Brave will not open any new tabs except when opened from the context menu (right-click menu).

Steps to Reproduce (add as many as necessary):  1. Launch Brave 2. Visit any website, then press CTRL + T (or CMD + T) to open a new tab 3. Repeat for additional ways tabs are opened - clicking on the + sign on tab bar,     from main menu, etc.

Actual Result (gifs and screenshots are welcome!): New tab is not opened

Expected Result: A new tab should be opened

Reproduces how often: Always

Brave Version(See the About Brave page in the main menu): Brave release - v0.60.0

Additional information: I’m using macOS Mojave v 10.1.14

Additional explanation

For users who are new to bug reporting and open source development, I’ve outlined the type of information to include when filling out each section of the template:

  1. Description of the Issue While it may seem obvious, this section will comprise the bulk of your report and not all descriptions are useful. We encourage anyone reporting provide as much detail about the issue in question as possible. Bad Description Example: “Some videos work in Brave.”  Good Description Example: “Youtube videos won’t play in Brave. When attempting to stream the player stays black and the loading symbol spins infinitely. When trying with Shields down, the ad before the video will play, but the actual content continues to load infinitely once the ad is done.”

     

  2. Steps to Reproduce It is often useful to know the exact steps taken that produce the behavior you detailed in your description of the issue. STR is different from the issue description in that it’s comprised of a numbered list of clearly defined and easy to follow actions that one would execute that produce the issue described. Example:      1. Launch Brave     2. Navigate to YouTube     3. Try to stream a video     4. Turn Shields off and try streaming again

     

  3. Actual Result This is the result you see after performing the above steps on your end. Almost like a short form version of your issue. Example: With Shields up video player shows loading screen forever - with shields down, ad before video plays, then returns to loading screen forever. 

     

  4. Expected result This is what you (specifically) thinkshouldbe happening after performing the above steps. Example: The selected video streams.  

  5. Brave Version Knowing what Brave build and version number you’re using can help see whether or not the issue is new, known, or a previously known bug that was resolved but is now appearing again (regression). It also confirms whether or not your browser has the latest updates and fixes which may be the cause of the bug. You can find your version and build information by going to selecting About Brave from the Main menu. Example: Version 0.55.22 Chromium: 70.0.3538.77 (Official Build) (64-bit)

     

  6. Additional Information Any additional details you’d like to add or comments to make once the above sections are filled you can put here. Screen shots or screen recordings are also particularly valuable when diagnosing an issue although they’re certainly not required. If you choose to include them in your report leave them here.

    Please provide information in as many sections as possible to help us resolve or log your issue as efficiently as possible. The entirety of the example issue used above is ~530 characters total (less than two Tweets!).

    NOTE: Any “One liner”, overtly vague, or bug reports/support requests that otherwise entirely ignore the above guidelines will not be responded to. Repeatedly posting such articles will get you flagged or banned. 

How do I submit photos for consideration on the New Tab Page?

If you’re a photographer and would like to submit your photos to be considered for the New Tab Page, please send an email with the subject line “New Tab Submission” to the design team.

Include your portfolio, the name for photo attribution, and a link you’d like to include as part of the photo attribution (optional). The link is a webpage or form that people will land on if they click on your photo attribution name in the bottom left corner of the New Tab page. Most photographers put their portfolio or some method of contacting them for future work, but it can be anything you want!

Images that are chosen must be high resolution - at least 3500px wide. Images should not contain any people or sensitive material.

We receive so many submissions that we won’t be able to reply individually but they will be considered for future inclusion.

What is Brave Community?

The Brave Community is a forum where people who care about the internet and their browsing experience come to discuss with each other. We’re here to help each other with issues and to make Brave, and the internet, better.

More specifically it’s the place to go to file bug reports, speak directly with Brave and contribute back to the Brave initiative in a more impactful way.

Desktop Browser: Brave Features

How do I use Brave News?

The Brave News reader is accessible below the new tab page and is delivered anonymously to the user’s browser via Brave’s new private content delivery network (CDN). Please see our official blog post for a full description of the feature. 

How do I enable/disable Brave News?

Brave News can be enabled or disabled by clicking the Customize button on the bottom of the New Tab Page. You can also reach this menu by going to Menu --> Settings --> New Tab Page --> Customize.... Once enabled, you can access and read your Brave News feed on the New Tab Page by simply scrolling down:

How do I manage what content appears in my feed?

From the customize Brave News screen, you can adjust Brave News settings, add or remove content sources, channels and RSS feeds. Use the toggle at the top of this screen to enable or disable Brave News. You may also use the drop down menu to choose where you want News links to open.

Brave News comes pre-packaged with a variety of sources and websites to add to your feed (note that some of these sources will be enabled by default). Some popular choices are displayed on the front page under the “Popular” section (note that you can use the arrow to scroll to the right to view additional popular sources).

Click the View All button to see all of the available pre-packaged sources you can add to your feed. To add or remove sources that appear in your feed, click the + button on the source you would like to add (or the - button to remove that source). Once added, the source will appear on the left side of the screen under “Following”:

Additionally, rather than adding individual sources for News to pull content from, you can instead add Channels. Adding a “Channel” will instead pull content relevant to that Channel from a variety of the available sources. For example, adding the Sports channel will pull content from sites like ESPN, Sports Illustrated, and CBS Sports, while adding the Gaming channel will pull content from sites like IGN, Gamespot and PC Gamer. Channels can be found on the main screen of the Brave News dashboard and are added the same way as individual sources, using the + button on the relevant Channel icon. Added Channels will also appear in the “Following” section:

 

Once sources/channels have been added, your feed will continue to tune itself as Brave will rank and curate content based on your source settings and browsing activity. Note that this is all done anonymously and without any of your data leaving your machine.

You may also add custom sites and RSS feeds that are not pre-packaged with Brave by using the Search bar at the top of the customize screen. Simply add a site URL or RSS address into the search bar and click on the desired result to add this content to your feed:

How do I use Brave Sidebar?

Brave Sidebar allows users to customize their browsing experience from a single panel, located on the side of the browser window.

Enabling Sidebar allows users to manage bookmarks with a new bookmarks panel, add shortcuts to their favorite websites, and allows quick access to Brave Talk and Brave Wallet. 

How do I enable Sidebar?

Brave Sidebar can be enabled in main menu of the browser as well as in Settings --> Appearance --> Sidebar:

(Enable side bar using main menu)

(Enable side bar in Settings)

The browser can be set to display Sidebar in two different modes:

  • Always - This mode will display the sidebar on the left side of the browser at all times for quick and easy access to any items added to it.
  • On mouseover - This mode will display the Sidebar only when the cursor is moved to the left side of the browser window. When moved away, the Sidebar will disappear until you move the cursor back to the left side of the browser window again.
  • Never - This essentially disables Sidebar and it will not show until one of the above modes is selected.

How do I customize items on the Sidebar?

Brave Sidebar has a few shortcut options enabled by default (listed from top to bottom):

  • Brave Leo — This shortcut will open the Brave Leo panel. Please see our Help Center articles on Brave Leo for more information on how to use Brave’s own privacy preserving AI.
  • Brave Wallet — This shortcut allows easy access to your Brave Wallet.
  • Brave Talk — This shortcut takes you to talk.brave.com to quickly start a Brave Talk meeting.
  • Bookmarks — The Bookmarks shortcut actually opens an additional panel, allowing you to easily open, organize or edit your bookmarks without having to leave the screen you’re on. Right-click on any bookmark item to edit, rename, add or remove your bookmarks:
To add new items to the Sidebar:

  1. Visit the site or page you would like to add

  2. Click the + icon on the sidebar — you will see the Add to Sidebar pop-up:

  3. Click on the site name that appears and the site will be added to the Sidebar for quick access:

To remove items from the Sidebar:

To remove any sites or pages on your Sidebar, simply right-click on the icon and select Remove:

To arrange items on the Sidebar:

Simply click and drag icons up or down on the sidebar to organize them to your liking:

How do I use Brave Translate?

💡Looking for How to use Translate on iOS? See this article here.

Brave browser now offers it’s own built-in translation feature for use in the Desktop and Android browser (iOS to be supported in future builds). Brave has partnered with Lingvanex to bring quick, quality and private in-page translation for 108 different languages to the browser.

Note that, as stated in our Privacy Policy, Brave removes IP addresses associated with requests submitted to the translation service and any text submitted is not retained after the request completes.

Using Extensions for Translate

While Brave Translate will be the default translation option, you may still use your desired Translation extension for translation services in the browser. We do recommend looking at the translations privacy policy to stay informed about what these extensions do with your translation data/requests. By default, any currently installed and enabled translation extension will override the built in translation feature. In order to use the Brave Translate feature, you’ll need to disable any translation extensions (you can do this in brave://settings/extensions).

Using Brave Translate

Simply visit any website that contains text in a foreign language and observe the Translate prompt appear in the address bar:

Note that visiting sites with text in a language set as a Preferred Language (these can be found in brave://settings/languages) will not display the Translate option. For example, the translation option would not appear when visiting the site in the image above if the German was included in the Preferred languages setting:

If you would like the browser to offer you the option to translate pages that display in one of your preferred languages anyway, you can do so by going to brave://settings/languages, selecting the “more options” menu (three dots icon) for the specific language and checking the Offer to translate pages in this language option:

Once prompted, click on the Translate bubble in the address bar to select which language you would like to translate the text into:

In the example above, selecting English will change any text on the site from German to English. You may also select the “More options”/“Translate Menu” to reveal additional options for translating the site. The options are as follows (note that the language used in this example is “German” but will reflect the relevant language):

  • Choose Another Language…: Allows you to select a different language to translate the site into on the fly.
  • Always Translate German: Tells the translation feature to always translate pages into german automatically (without the need to select the prompt again).
  • Never Translate German: Tells the translation feature to never translate the language the site is displayed in for any site.
  • Never Translate This Site: Tells the translation feature to never translate this specific website’s text.
  • Page Is Not in German: Tells the translation feature that it has detected the wrong language and prompts you to select the correct language the site is displayed in.

You may also translate a page from it’s native text to your desired text via the context menu when right-clicking on the page:
