To start using Brave Wallet on desktop, open the Brave Browser and click the icon in the toolbar. To get started with Brave Wallet on mobile, open the browser menu and then tap the icon.

How do I send crypto in Brave Wallet?

  1. In Brave, click the  icon in the browser toolbar.
  2. Enter your password to unlock your secure wallet.
  3. Select send in the wallet panel.

The below screen will appear in your wallet. Select the Choose Asset option.

Choose the NFT or token you wish to send and the amount.

Enter the address of the recipient or pick from a list of your addresses. We recommend that you copy and paste the address rather than typing it by hand. This helps to avoid mistakes and potential loss of funds.

Another best practice is to check the first and last four digits of the address, once it’s been pasted, alongside where it was copied from to make sure it matches. If it’s a large transaction, it may also be wise to first send a test transaction to confirm it’s going to the right place.

Once ready, double check the address one last time and review the transaction fees. If everything looks correct, confirm the transaction to post it to the blockchain and initiate the transfer.

To get started with Brave Wallet on desktop, open the Brave Browser and click the  icon in the toolbar. To get started with Brave Wallet on mobile, open the browser menu and then tap the  icon.

What is the Associated Token Account Program?

The Associated Token Account Program on Solana automatically creates a token account involving the sending or receiving of a new asset.

For example, when you send SPL-BAT to a new address, the token account program ensures that a corresponding SPL-BAT account is created for you on the receiving address. If it doesn’t exist, a small amount of SOL will be spent to create and fund the new SPL-BAT token account.

You can learn more here.

Zcash and Address Types

Zcash is a secure digital currency that helps protect your privacy. With Zcash, there are two types of addresses:

  • Transparent addresses: Transactions with transparent addresses, or t-addresses, can be tracked on the Zcash blockchain the same way Bitcoin can.
  • Shielded addresses: Shielded addresses, or z-addresses, use zero-knowledge proofs to hide the sender, receiver, and amount of a transaction from the public blockchain.

If a t-address sends funds to a z-address, observers won’t be able to tell where they went. If a z-address sends a transaction to another z-address the transaction is entirely shielded from prying eyes, offering one of the most private and secure options on the market.

Brave Wallet supports shielded addresses in 1.77x and above. Android and iOS are unavailable at this time.

Wallet: Trading Assets with Brave Swaps

Brave Swaps FAQ

What data does Brave Wallet have on Swaps?

Brave does not collect data on individual users as part of this feature. See our privacy policy here.

What is 0x Api (https://docs.0x.org)?

0x is an open-source, decentralized exchange infrastructure that enables the exchange of tokenized assets on multiple blockchains. The 0x protocol is, at its core, a set of secure smart contracts that facilitate the peer-to-peer exchange of Ethereum-based assets. The protocol serves as an open standard and common building block for any developer needing exchange functionality.

What can 0x Api see?

0x will process the Ethereum address and IP address to fulfill a transaction (including getting quotes). 0x will only use this data for the purposes of processing transactions.

What is Jupiter (https://docs.jup.ag/)?

Jupiter is a DEX aggregator on the Solana Blockchain. Brave Wallet utilizes Jupiter for providing liquidity for different tokens on Solana.

What can Jupiter see?

Jupiter will process the Solana address and IP address to fulfill a transaction, this is also true for getting a quote. Jupiter will only use this data for the purposes of processing transactions. Jupiter doesn’t store any data outside of errors where they will log time, region and error.

How do I bridge tokens in Brave Wallet?

What is a bridge?

A bridge is a service that enables the transfer of digital assets between different blockchain networks. When you have funds or tokens on one blockchain, you can use a bridge to transfer them to another eligible network of your choice.

 

To start using Brave Wallet on desktop, open the Brave Browser and click the icon in the toolbar. To get started with Brave Wallet on mobile, open the browser menu and then tap the icon.

How do I change the quote provider?

Each aggregator provides quotes by using liquidity from its API. They gather price information from various exchanges and offer the prices based on this data. Brave automatically chooses the best quote provider. However, you can manually change your provider for a Brave Swap.

 

  1. In Brave, click the  icon in the browser toolbar.
  2. Enter your password to unlock your secure wallet.
  3. Click the swap icon in the panel.
  4. Find the Brave logo located in the middle of the panel.
  5. Select your desired quote provider from the list.

Need help with swapping an asset? Click here.

How do I swap tokens with Brave Wallet?

Swap from one asset to another using Brave’s built-in swap aggregator. Swaps are currently available for Ethereum, Solana, and many EVM-compatible chains.

  1. In Brave, click the  icon in the browser toolbar.
  2. Enter your password to unlock your secure wallet.

Your wallet will unlock and a panel appears, showing your assets at a glance. Click the swap icon in the panel.

 

First, choose the appropriate asset and the account on which you would like to make the Brave Swap.

 

.

Select the assets you want to swap from and receive, and the amount to swap. Brave provides a few options for dex aggregators, which search for the best possible exchange rates across a variety of decentralized exchanges.

Review the order for swapping. Depending on the blockchain network, you may need to sign a transaction prior to the swap in order to give approval for the swap tool to use the tokens in your wallet. Brave Wallet will walk you through this process.

Confirm the transaction. Once the swap has been configured and initiated, all that’s left to do is confirm. Review all the details of your swap and the estimated balance change. This is the point of no return. If everything looks good to you, click Confirm.

Your tokens have now been swapped! After completing the swap, you’ll get a link to a block explorer where you can view expanded transaction details, and a time estimate or confirmation for the transaction settlement.

What are Brave Swaps?

In Brave Wallet, swaps refers to the exchanging of one token for another.

A crypto swap is a transaction that allows you to exchange one token for another without having to go through a centralized exchange. In a Brave Swap, you essentially trade one cryptocurrency for another, and the transaction is settled on a decentralized exchange (DEX).

Brave provides a few options for decentralized exchange aggregators, which searches for the best possible exchange rates across a variety of decentralized exchanges. By using an aggregator for swaps, this helps with the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the swaps, and minimizes the amount of slippage and overall transaction fees.

Wallet: Web3 Wallet Settings

Adding a New Chain

Brave Wallet automatically provides a list of the most popular networks used in Web3. However, if you do not see a desired network available, you can add a custom network from your Web3 settings.

Click on the main menu (  ), choose Settings > Web3. Alternatively, you can enter brave://settings/web3 in your address bar.

Select the Wallet Networks option.

Click Add in the top-right.

Next, you can search for the network from the list provided or enter the details manually. 

 

Click Submit once all details have been entered.

Adjusting the Default Wallet

Dapps work by communicating with a special object called window.ethereum. Brave Wallet and extensions like MetaMask use this object to help connect you to dApps. However, only one wallet can provide window.ethereum to websites. In Brave, we expose a setting in brave://settings/web3 to be able to change which wallet provides window.ethereum. Here’s a description of each setting:

  • Extensions (Brave Wallet fallback) - This is the default. Brave Wallet will expose window.ethereum but allow other extensions such as MetaMask to overwrite it.
  • Brave Wallet - Exposes window.ethereum and prevents sites and extensions from changing window.ethereum.
  • Crypto Wallets (Deprecated) - Gives access to the old deprecated wallet. This option is not compatible with other extensions such as MetaMask.
  • Extensions (no fallback) - window.ethereum will not be provided by Brave Wallet at all. If you have extensions such as MetaMask, it is free to use window.ethereum.

After changing the default wallet, it is best to refresh your browser or dApp page. Why?

  • If you had Brave Wallet loaded, it won’t be unloaded until the next refresh. When Brave Wallet is loaded it will not work properly with other extensions trying to access window.ethereum.
  • An existing already opened tab will not change to use the new wallet setting, you will need a new tab or a page refresh.

Changing the Default RPC Node

Brave proxy calls blockchain RPC providers so they can’t track you when using Brave Wallet. Brave users have the option to change their default RPC node as well.

Click on the main menu (  ), choose Settings > Web3. Alternatively, you can enter brave://settings/web3 in your address bar.

Select the Wallet Networks option.

Find the network of the RPC node you’d like to change. Click on the three dots and select Edit.

Click on the (+) sign to the right of the RPC URLs section. Enter the URL of the RPC you’d like to set.

Confirm the correct RPC is selected and click Submit.

Hiding Brave Wallet

Brave Wallet is built-in to the browser, but you can disable functionality and remove it from view in your browser toolbar.

To hide the Brave Wallet icon in the toolbar, you can use the Customize Toolbar option in Settings → Appearance. Or you can right-click the icon and select Hide.

 

Note: You can use Group Policy to disable Wallet at the administrative level. You can also remove the Wallet icon from the browser sidebar.

Resetting Brave Wallet

Please note, Brave can NOT access your wallet or reverse a wallet reset. The recovery phrase is the ONLY way to regain access if the wallet is reset.

Click on the main menu ( ), choose Settings > Web3. Alternatively, you can enter brave://settings/web3 in your address bar.

Select the Reset and clear wallet data option at the bottom.

A window will appear confirming your decision to reset the wallet. Type Yes in the available box and click OK to reset.

A message will appear confirming the wallet was reset successfully.

Resolve Methods for Unstoppable Domains

This page describes the resolve methods Brave supports for resolving domain names when visiting Unstoppable Domains (ex: .crypto domains). Users can find the setting by visiting brave://settings/web3 and look for Resolve Unstoppable Domains domain names.

 

  • Ask: This is the default option which Brave would ask whether to enable Unstoppable Domains support when visiting .crypto domains.
  • Disabled: Disable the support of Unstoppable Domains.
  • Enabled: Brave will be using Infura to issue Ethereum JSON-RPC call to the smart contract from Unstoppable Domains to resolve .crypto domain name lookup requests. If you enable this, Infura will see the .crypto domain that you’re trying to visit but they will not be able to see other domains. See Infura’s terms of use and privacy policy.

Android Browser: Miscellaneous

How do I customize the New Tab Page on Android?

Brave allows you to customize elements of the New Tab Page in the Android browser to suit your browsing needs. Note that further customization options will be available in future releases.

Top Sites

Top Sites on the New Tab Page appear beneath the Privacy stats and allow quick access to the sites you visit the most. At this time, the sites listed here are auto-populated based on the most frequently visited sites. Tapping on the icon will launch the site in the tab you’re currently on. Note that you may scroll left-right on this strip to view additional sites on the strip.

If you long press (tap and hold) on a site icon, additional options will appear allowing you to select where the site is opened, as well as allow you to remove a site from the list of Top Sites.

   

Enable or disable New Tab Page elements

You can adjust what shows on the New Tab Page by navigating to Main Menu --> Settings --> Display --> New Tab Page in the browser:

  • Show Background Images: Toggling this option on/off will enable or disable the browser from displaying the built-in background images that come with the browser. 
  • Show Sponsored Images: Toggling this option on/off will enable or disable the browser from displaying the New Tab Page sponsored images which you can use to earn BAT from through the Brave Rewards program. 
  • Show Top Sites: Toggle this option on/off to show or hide the Top Sites strip on the new tab page. Note that disabling this option will note remove top sites from the list.
  • Show Brave Stats: Toggling this option on or off allows you to display or hide the Brave Privacy stats on the New Tab Page.

How do I install Brave on Android?

Please see the How do I download and install Brave? article for installation instructions and system requirements for all Brave platforms.

How do I use tab groups on Android?

Tab groups allow you to better organize your list of open tabs. A group can have any number of tabs contained within it and each group of tabs will display as a single tab window in the tabs view:

Two tab groups and to regular tabs

You can create a tab group by:

  • Opening the main menu and tapping Add tab to group, which will add the current tab to the desired group or create a new tab group, starting with the current tab.
  • Tapping the overflow menu when viewing all open tabs and selecting New tab group
  • Long-pressing on an open tab and selecting Add tab to group from the context menu

When creating a new tab group, you will be prompted to name the group if desired, as well as select a color to associate with the group (note that these can be changed at any time):

You can tap the tab groups button when viewing your open tabs to display all current tab groups you have open in the browser:

Tapping on a tab group in the tabs view will show the group in it’s own window, allowing you to scroll through all open tabs contained within.

Note that you can also rearrange tabs here by long-pressing and dragging the tab to the desired position. From this view, you can also:

  • Open a new tab within this group in this view by tapping the + icon.
  • Edit the tab group title by tapping on the title at the top of the group.
  • Change the tab group color by tapping on the colored circle left of the group title.
  • Use the overflow menu to do all of the above, as well as delete the group and close all tabs contained within.

When viewing an individual tab that is part of a group, a tab strip will display at the bottom of the screen, showing other tabs that are a part of this group. Tap any of these icons to switch to it.

You can also open a new tab here by tapping the + icon on the strip

By default, Brave will open links in new tabs outside of the current group. However, you can set the browser to automatically open links inside the current tab group by going to Settings --> Appearance and toggling the Only open links in current tab group option “on”.

iOS Browser: Miscellaneous

How do I manage Shields and Privacy settings on iOS?

Brave on iOS allows you to configure your default Shields settings and manage other private data the same way you can on Desktop and Android. You can find more information on Brave Shields here. 

Brave Shields & Privacy

You can find Shields and Privacy settings on the iOS application:

  1. In Brave, tap Menu --> All Settings --> Shields & Privacy. Alternatively, you can click on the Brave Shields icon and navigate to Change Shields Global Defaults.

 

Brave Shields Global Defaults

The top section in Brave Shields & Privacy are the default protections that Shields will use when visiting websites. The default settings are optimized for user protection and minimal conflicts. These settings can be adjusted to meet individual needs.

Note: Changing these settings won’t affect your existing per-site settings. 

Clear Private Data

You can clear browser data such as Browsing History, Cookies and more. Choose the data types you would like to remove, then tap Clear Data Now. This action cannot be reversed.

Other Privacy Settings

The last section contains additional privacy and security settings which can be customized based on user preferences.

  • Private Browsing Only Toggling this option On will tell the browser to only open private windows when the browser is launched. The browser will behave this way until the setting is toggled Off. Please see our Private Browsing section for more information on what Private windows are and how they function.
  • Block `Switch to App` Notices Enabling this setting will prevent the “open-in-app” notices from appearing. You can learn more about Switch to App prompts here. 
  • Allow universal links to open in external apps Enabling this option will open links in external apps when applicable.
  • Block Popups This option is set to On by default. This prevents websites from opening new browser windows/tabs without your permission. We recommend keeping this option On.
  • Block Dangerous Wesites This option is set to On by default. This protection will reference the Google Safe browsing service (note that these connections are always proxied so that your personal/system information is never sent to Google directly) which is used to track, flag and warn a user when sites are known to be potentially malicious or harmful. We recommend keeping this option On.
